reasons: Deviation classification is sound: Section 13.1 affirmatively excludes Affiliates and contractors from the Services licence ('Customer alone ... without Affiliates or contractors') with no notice-based path to add them, which fails even the fallback (affiliates covered on written notice) and sits in walk-away territory alongside revocation at Vendor's sole discretion.

Sections 13.2 and 13.3 do not cure the gap: 13.2 is limited to paid-up/embedded software and Vendor Technology, and 13.3 addresses revocation and transfer only, not the scope of the Services grant. The rationale correctly acknowledges 13.3's revocation constraint rather than overstating the breach.

The redline reaches the preferred position (Affiliates plus contractors acting on our behalf, revocation/suspension only per the notice-and-cure standard in 13.3, transfer to an Affiliate or successor) and does so by cross-referencing terms already agreed in 13.3 rather than importing new concessions.

The advisory changed-character ratio (0.746) is justified: the original sentence is affirmatively exclusionary, so the exclusion cannot be fixed by insertion alone and the clause must be recast; the edit stays within one sentence and preserves the licensed subject matter (the Services).
Comment is accurate, correctly prefixed, first person plural, explains both changes, cites the playbook position, and offers the written-notice fallback without lecturing.
